Participant-by-candidate log-likelihood matrix

Source: R/likelihood.R
trajectory_loglik.Rd

Scores every participant against every candidate trajectory, giving the matrix \(\log p_k(Y_i \mid \theta_m)\) that fit_bank() and class_loglik() consume. This is the only place the mechanistic model enters: trajectory can be any function of time and a parameter row.

Usage

trajectory_loglik(
  obs,
  candidates,
  trajectory,
  sigma,
  lags = NULL,
  lag_prior = NULL
)

Arguments

obs

A data frame with one row per measurement and columns id, time, value, and optionally censored and lod.

candidates

A data frame or matrix of candidate parameter values, one row per candidate.

trajectory

A function (time, theta) returning the trajectory value at time for the single candidate theta (one row of candidates).

sigma

Residual standard deviation on the \(\log_{10}\) scale.

lags

Optional numeric vector of candidate time shifts, in the units of obs$time. When the clock on which measurements are recorded is not the biological clock – days since a reported symptom onset rather than days since infection – the offset is unknown and must be integrated out rather than fixed. Each observation time is evaluated at time + lag.

lag_prior

Prior weights over lags, normalised internally. Defaults to uniform.

Value

A numeric matrix with one row per participant (named by id) and one column per candidate, with any lag already marginalised out.

See also

fit_bank(), class_loglik(), background_loglik()

Examples

obs <- data.frame(id = rep(1:2, each = 3), time = rep(c(1, 3, 6), 2),
                  value = c(100, 60, 20, 500, 300, 90))
cand <- data.frame(rate = c(0.1, 0.3), peak = c(200, 600))
decay <- function(t, th) th$peak * exp(-th$rate * t)
trajectory_loglik(obs, cand, decay, sigma = 0.3)
#>         [,1]       [,2]
#> 1 -3.4072977 -6.2245675
#> 2 -0.7899403  0.7858733

## with an unknown infection time, integrated over a one-day grid
trajectory_loglik(obs, cand, decay, sigma = 0.3, lags = -2:2)
#>         [,1]      [,2]
#> 1 -3.0718806 -3.173365
#> 2 -0.7558832  0.337751
